newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO REMAINS GOAL SHY AS BARCELONA EDGE HOME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO REMAINS GOAL SHY AS BARCELONA EDGE HOME.

text.p: Barcelona closed on Spanish league leaders Real Madrid on Sunday with a scrappy 1-0 home win over Celta Vigo. Even Ronaldo was jeered.
Barcelona trail Real by two points and occupy second place on goal difference from Deportivo Coruna, who drew 1-1 at Sporting Gijon. Real returned from Valladolid on Saturday with the same result.

Barcelona's game did not prompt the demonstrations against club management which had been expected after a week of dressing room upheavals, but fans became unhappy when captain Gheorghe Popescu missed a first-half penalty. A goal by Miguel Angel Nadal sealed the points.
Coach Bobby Robson tried to justify Ronaldo's performance afterwards by detailing every attack made by the Brazilian, who has gone four games without scoring.

Other unhappy supporters could be found at Zaragoza -- languishing in the relegation zone after the 2-0 defeat by Racing Santander -- and Atletico Madrid, where followers carried banners criticising media treatment of their team. The Spanish champions fought back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with Real Sociedad.
Atletico stayed fifth, 10 points off the pace, and six behind Real Betis, who dispatched beleaguered neighbours Sevilla 3-0 in a rain-affected derby.

Sevilla coach Jose Antonio Camacho was expected to re-submit his resignation after the humiliating defeat, having already seen an earlier attempt to quit rejected by club president Jose Maria Gonzalez.
Gonzalez was not at the game, but is under considerable pressure himself because of a series of embarrassing financial scandals at the club.

For Sevilla -- third from bottom in a season in which four clubs are relegated aotomatically -- the postive note was struck by Croatian midfielder Robert Prosinecki and Danish defender Thomas Rytter, who turned in fine debut performances.
A hat-trick by Felipe Minambres helped Tenerife to a spectacular 5-1 win over Espanyol, while Logrones sank further into trouble after losing 2-0 at home to Racing Santander.
Deportivo's game at Sporting Gijon was overshadowed by an injury to French striker Mickael Madar, out for four months after breaking his leg.
Former international forward Julio Salinas bade farewell to the Spanish league by scoring the equaliser for Sporting.
The strike made Salinas the highest-scoring Spanish striker still playing, lifting him ahead of former team mate Jose Maria Bakero, who recently left Barcelona for Mexico.
Salinas is set to move to Japan after playing for Athletic Bilbao, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and Deportivo Coruna.
But he will not be remembered with fondness by most Spanish fans, who blame him for missing several key chances for the national side.
